## Step 1: Understand the purpose of a write-ahead log
A write-ahead log (WAL) is a mechanism used by databases to ensure data consistency and durability in the event of a system crash or failure. The primary purpose of a WAL is to record all changes made to the database before they are written to the main database files.

## Step 2: Explain the structure of the log file
The log file is structured as a sequence of log records, each of which represents a single database operation, such as a write or update. Each log record contains a sequence number, the type of operation (e.g., insert, update, delete), and any relevant data required to perform the operation. The log records are written in a specific order to ensure that they can be applied in a consistent manner.

In this statement, a "crash" is a situation in which the database is shut down abruptly (e.g. due to a power outage, a server failure, or a bug in the software).
A write-ahead log (WAL) is a record of all modifications made to a database. When a modification is made to a database, the change is first written to the log, and then it is applied to the database. This ensures that the log is always up-to-date, even if the database itself is not. If the database crashes, the WAL can be used to recover the database to its previous state.
When the database crashes, the WAL contains a record of all the modifications that were made, but not yet written to the database. These modifications can be reapplied to the database, restoring it to its previous state. This process is called recovery.
